events.title: Massachusetts Issues the Western Hemisphere's First Paper Money
events.description: After a failed expedition against Quebec and a near-mutiny among unpaid soldiers, the Massachusetts Bay Colony authorized paper currency to pay its troops.
events.significance: This was the first government-issued paper money in the Western Hemisphere. It anticipated the paper currencies that later became standard worldwide.

events.title: Poet Emily Dickinson Is Born
events.description: Emily Dickinson was born in Amherst, Massachusetts. She lived a largely secluded life and wrote close to 1,800 poems, most of them unpublished while she was alive.
events.significance: Her compact, unconventional verse about death, nature and the inner life made her one of America's most celebrated poets.

events.title: The First Nobel Prizes Are Awarded
events.description: On the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death, the first Nobel Prizes were presented in Stockholm. They honored achievements in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature and peace, as his will directed.
events.significance: The ceremony began a tradition of honoring human achievement that continues every December 10.

events.title: Edward VIII Signs the Instrument of Abdication
events.description: Britain's King Edward VIII signed the documents giving up the throne so that he could marry the twice-divorced American Wallis Simpson. His brother became King George VI.
events.significance: It was the only voluntary abdication of a British monarch. It reshaped the royal line of succession and put the future Queen Elizabeth II on course to reign.

events.title: The UN Adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
events.description: The United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Paris. It set out fundamental rights that every person is entitled to.
events.significance: It became a foundation for international human rights law. The date is now observed each year as Human Rights Day.
